thread:
maya: Heads-up — River13b onboarding hitting weird mem/latency behavior on prefetch+adaptive-batching. Canary saw 3x p95 and a couple of GPU OOMs when users request long outputs (>512).
aj: Ugh. Is this the int4 quant build?
maya: yeah int4 qdkl build + KV prefetch enabled by default. baseline perf looked fine on unit tests but in canary real traffic shows a pattern: latency climbs mostly on sequences with many short turns, and OOMs correlate with high max_new_tokens requests.
liam: do we have logs for the OOM stack? any kv-trim events?
sophie: @maya can you paste the canary summary link?
maya: sure — https://go/reports/river13b-canary (private) — key snippets below:

```
[2026-03-20 18:12:05] alloc_failure: Allocation 2.1GB failed during kv_prefetch, current_used=11.8GB, reserved_pool=12GB
[2026-03-20 18:12:05] kv_cache: prefetching 60KB chunk x 48
[2026-03-20 18:12:05] batch: size=12 max_new_tokens=1024
```

maya: TL;DR: aggressive prefetch + large max_new_tokens + mid-size batches => transient fragmentation + huge contiguous alloc requests for kv blocks.
aj: hypothesis: prefetch is pulling a lot of KV pages upfront and with int4 the allocator fragmentation causes large contiguous allocations to fail. Also batch size 12+ with 1024 max_new is rare but when it hits it spikes.
liam: we should try two mitigations in parallel: 1) lower default max_new_tokens to 256 for River13b int4 canary, 2) change kv_prefetch to 'bounded' mode that caps total prefetch bytes per-request.
sophie: agree. Also add a temporary soft throttle that forces batch size<=8 for requests with max_new_tokens>256. That reduces concurrent kv working set.
maya: I'll open a tiny patch for service defaults and a canary override. Patch diff in comment: 

```
# service config snippet
models:
  river13b-int4:
    defaults:
      max_new_tokens: 256
      kv_prefetch: bounded
      kv_prefetch_max_bytes: 65536 # per request
    batch:
      max_batch_size: 8
      dynamic_batching: true
```

aj: can we also try forcing KV eviction earlier (lower threshold) so we don't attempt large contiguous allocations? e.g., set kv_eviction_threshold_pct=70 instead of 85.
liam: yea, lowering to 70 should free slots proactively. Also we should instrument fragmentation metrics: largest_free_segment_bytes, free_chunks_count.
sophie: I can add those to console dashboards under river13b.int4.prefetch.* so we can correlate.
maya: running the canary with these three changes now — will report back in ~20m.
deploy-bot: deploy started for config river13b-int4 @ canary pool-7 (uid: d33f9) :rocket:
maya: quick note — reduced default tokens already dropped p95 ~35% in first 5 minutes. no OOMs so far. fragment metric shows median largest_free_segment_bytes rose from 1.8GB -> 3.2GB (good).
aj: nice. Any quality regression from lowering max_new_tokens? should be fine for most callers but check eval set.
maya: ran eval on long-dialog set: slight drop on recall@top for extremely long completions (expected). we have a fallback policy to route requests that need >512 tokens to dedicated pool with larger reserved slots — did not trigger yet.
liam: next step: add transient compact-on-alloc for the runtime path that handles failed contiguous allocations: attempt background compaction up to X ms then retry. That might prevent OOMs without reducing defaults.
sophie: we'll need an SRE signoff for compaction CPU cost. pinging @aj for impact assessment.
aj: ack. if canary stays green for 2 hours with current defaults we'll roll to stable with a note. Also create a short doc for customers about the new default max_new_tokens and recommended path for long-run outputs.
maya: will do. saving logs + canary timeline to the incident bucket. thanks all :+1:
liam: filing a follow-up ticket to explore allocator-level fixes (slab merging heuristics) — lower priority but probably needed long-term.
maya: update (20m): canary 1h in, p95 back to baseline, no further OOMs. Closing the urgent triage. I'll keep the config change for one day then propose stable rollout.
sophie: closing loop: dashboards and alert thresholds updated. adding an automated canary test to exercise large max_new_tokens paths nightly.
maya: good work. saved notes to the onboarding playbook.
